topic: The Art of Dimensional Shifting: Geometry Beyond the Flat
target_audience: High school students and geometry enthusiasts

sections.title: The Ant's Dilemma: Introduction to Dimensional Constraints
lecture_lines: Meet our ant, trapped inside a flat 2D circle.
To the ant, this boundary is an impassable wall.
But a new axis offers a path through height.
The ant leaps over the once-solid barrier.
It lands safely on the other side.
animations: Show a 2D plane with a red circle (#FF0000) and a green dot 'Ant' (#00FF00) inside.
The green dot (#00FF00) moves to the circle edge, stops, and shakes to show it's stuck.
A blue arrow (#0000FF) tilted at 45 degrees appears to represent the Z-axis (height).
The green dot (#00FF00) scales up 1.5x and moves diagonally 'up and over' the circle line.
The green dot (#00FF00) scales back to 1.0x and settles on the plane outside the circle.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The 0D to 3D Ladder
lecture_lines: A zero-dimensional point marks a single location.
Stretching it creates lines, then flat 2D shapes.
Shifting into 3D transforms the square into a cube.
animations: A white point (#FFFFFF) appears in the center, labeled '0D: Point'.
The point stretches horizontally into a cyan line (#00FFFF) '1D', then vertically into a yellow square (#FFFF00) '2D'.
The square stretches diagonally into an isometric magenta cube (#FF00FF) labeled '3D: Space'.

sections.title: Puzzle 1: The Matchstick Triangle (The 2D to 3D Leap)
lecture_lines: Can six matchsticks form four equilateral triangles?
We can easily build one triangle in 2D.
But the remaining sticks fail to form more.
Lift the sticks into the third dimension instead.
Now, a 3D tetrahedron creates four perfect triangles.
animations: Six brown matchstick segments (#A52A2A) are scattered randomly on the screen.
Three segments form a single flat yellow triangle (#FFFF00) in the center.
The other three segments try to form triangles on the plane but overlap and fail.
The three segments lift and connect to a single point above the first triangle (isometric view).
The resulting 3D tetrahedron's four faces are highlighted in gold (#FFD700) and numbered 1-4.

sections.title: The 'Unfolding' Technique: 3D to 2D Projection
lecture_lines: Finding the shortest path across a cube is tricky.
Unfold the 3D surface into a flat 2D net.
Now, a simple straight line reveals the best route.
animations: Display a white isometric cube (#FFFFFF) with a red dot 'Spider' (#FF0000) and blue dot 'Fly' (#0000FF) at opposite corners.
The cube faces rotate and flatten out into a light grey 2D 'T-shape' net (#D3D3D3).
A straight green line (#00FF00) is drawn between the red and blue dots on the flat net.

sections.title: Topology Twist: The Möbius Strip
lecture_lines: Start with a simple, flat rectangular strip.
Add a half-twist to the center of the strip.
Joining the ends creates the famous Möbius loop.
Follow the path along its single continuous surface.
One journey visits both sides without crossing an edge.
animations: Show a long, flat white rectangular strip (#FFFFFF).
The strip's middle section narrows and changes shading to represent a 180-degree twist.
The ends of the twisted strip connect to form a blue Möbius loop (#00BFFF).
An orange dot (#FF4500) begins a slow traversal along the center of the Möbius loop.
The dot completes one full cycle, visiting what were both 'sides' before returning to start.

sections.title: Summary: The 'N+1' Mindset
lecture_lines: A 2D knot seems impossible to untie.
Lifting a loop into 3D releases the constraint.
Solve complex problems by seeking the next dimension.
animations: Show a tangled yellow loop (#FFD700) representing a knot constrained to 2D.
A cross-over point flashes white (#FFFFFF) as one segment lifts 'up' into the 3rd dimension to clear the other.
The knot unties into a green circle (#00FF00) with the text 'N+1: A New Perspective' (#FFFFFF).
